stories.title: XRP whales buy the dip as leverage outpaces spot 6-to-1, while ether shows deeper capitulation
stories.summary: XRP whales have kept accumulating through recent price weakness, even as leveraged trading volume in the token runs six times higher than spot volume, creating what CryptoSlate frames as a $2.36 billion risk exposure. CoinDesk reports that ether is showing more pronounced signs of capitulation than XRP over the same stretch.
stories.whyItMatters: A leverage-to-spot ratio this skewed raises the odds of sharp liquidation-driven moves, and the divergence between XRP whale buying and ether capitulation is a useful gauge of where risk is concentrated across majors.
whatToWatch: Whether the leverage-to-spot ratio in XRP normalizes or keeps widening
Continued on-chain whale accumulation data
Signs of stabilization or further capitulation in ether
questions: What's specifically driving XRP whale buying amid broader softness?
Could the heavy leverage trigger a cascading liquidation event?

stories.title: Ethereum staking token weETH pulls back from restaking as rewards debate intensifies
stories.summary: weETH, a liquid staking token built on ether, is reportedly distancing itself from the restaking model it was originally built around, according to CoinDesk, as debate grows over how staking rewards should be structured. Specifics on the change are still limited.
stories.whyItMatters: Restaking has been a major growth engine for Ethereum's staking ecosystem, so a shift away from it by a prominent token could signal broader repricing of risk in DeFi yield products.
whatToWatch: Further detail on what structurally is changing at weETH
Whether other restaking protocols follow or diverge
Any impact on restaking TVL
questions: What exactly is changing in weETH's design?
Is this an isolated move or the start of a broader retreat from restaking?

stories.title: Bitcoin whales load up on $1.2 billion in BTC as ETFs attract $750 million
stories.summary: Large bitcoin holders added roughly $1.2 billion worth of BTC while US spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in about $750 million in fresh inflows, according to CoinDesk.
stories.whyItMatters: Simultaneous whale accumulation and ETF inflows point to strengthening demand from both large individual holders and institutional channels, a combination that's historically been supportive for price.
whatToWatch: Whether the ETF inflow streak continues
Further whale wallet accumulation
Any reversal in either flow
questions: Do the whale purchases and ETF inflows trace back to overlapping buyers?
Is this pace of accumulation sustainable given current market conditions?

stories.title: Bitcoin wallet dormant since 2011 moves $3.2 million toward FalconX-linked address
stories.summary: A bitcoin wallet inactive since 2011 moved roughly $3.2 million worth of BTC toward an address linked to trading firm FalconX, according to CoinDesk.
stories.whyItMatters: Movements from long-dormant wallets are closely watched as potential signals of early-holder selling or institutional OTC activity, both of which can hint at shifting supply dynamics.
whatToWatch: Whether the funds are sold, moved again, or held static
Any statement from FalconX on the transfer
questions: Is this an early holder cashing out or a custody/OTC transfer?
Will other long-dormant wallets show similar movement?

stories.title: Coldcard fallout shows up on-chain as 210,000 bitcoin leaves old wallets
stories.summary: In the wake of a security issue involving hardware wallet maker Coldcard, roughly 210,000 bitcoin has moved out of long-dormant wallets, according to CoinDesk. The scale suggests holders are proactively migrating funds amid security concerns.
stories.whyItMatters: A security scare touching a hardware wallet used for self-custody, at a scale involving hundreds of thousands of bitcoin, is a significant operational-risk event for anyone holding crypto outside exchanges.
whatToWatch: Official details on the nature and scope of the Coldcard issue
Further wallet migrations in coming days
Any response from Coldcard or affected custody providers
questions: What exactly went wrong with Coldcard?
How many affected holders have moved funds versus how many remain exposed?

stories.title: Crypto market maker Wintermute lands SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks
stories.summary: Wintermute, a major crypto market maker, has received SEC approval to trade equities and ETF blocks, according to CoinDesk, extending its business beyond digital assets into traditional securities markets.
stories.whyItMatters: The approval reflects growing convergence between crypto-native trading firms and traditional finance, and suggests US regulators are becoming more open to letting crypto firms operate in conventional securities markets.
whatToWatch: How quickly Wintermute begins trading equities and ETF blocks
Whether other crypto market makers pursue similar approvals
questions: What specific registration or license did Wintermute obtain?
Does this mark a broader regulatory opening for crypto-native trading firms?

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,300 as traders await US jobs report, with oil a fresh headwind
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded roughly flat near $64,300 heading into Friday's US jobs report, with CoinDesk's live markets coverage citing rising oil prices as an added headwind for risk assets. That follows a similarly flat session on Thursday near $64,000.
stories.whyItMatters: Macro data releases like the jobs report remain a key near-term catalyst for bitcoin, and a resurgence in oil prices points to inflation and rate concerns that can weigh on risk appetite broadly.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin's reaction to the US jobs report
Whether price breaks out of its recent tight range
The trajectory of oil prices as a cross-asset headwind
questions: How would bitcoin react to a jobs report surprise in either direction?

stories.title: Ethereum volume plunged 73% on Bullish, but a 72% spread jump saved its monthly bottom line
stories.summary: Ether trading volume on the Bullish exchange fell 73%, but a 72% jump in bid-ask spreads helped the platform preserve its monthly revenue, according to CryptoSlate.
stories.whyItMatters: Falling volume alongside widening spreads points to thinning liquidity in ether markets even as exchange revenue holds steady — a divergence that matters for anyone trading size in the asset.
whatToWatch: Whether ether volumes recover on Bullish and other venues
Further movement in spreads
Bullish's next monthly disclosures
questions: Is the volume drop specific to Bullish or part of a broader ether liquidity slowdown?
